newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-WASIM HITS RECORD 12 SIXES IN UNBEATEN 257.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WASIM HITS RECORD 12 SIXES IN UNBEATEN 257.

text.p: Pakistan's captain Wasim Akram smashed a career-best unbeaten 257 and broke two world records on the fourth day of the first test against Zimbabwe on Sunday.
He pulverised the weak Zimbabwean bowling as Pakistan steam-rollered to 553 all out and a commanding first innings lead of 178.
At tea, the tourists were six without loss in their second innings.

Together with his overnight partner Saqlain Mushtaq, Akram put on a monumental 313 for the eighth wicket, which eclipsed the 65-year-old test record of 246 set by England's Les Ames and Gubby Allen against New Zealand at Lord's in 1931.
Akram, in his marathon knock, cracked 22 fours and 12 sixes during 489 minutes at the crease, establishing a record for most sixes in a test.
The previous record was held by England's Wally Hammond, who hit 10 sixes in his 336 against New Zealand at Auckland in the 1932-33 series.
The Akram-Saqlain partnership was eventually broken by seamer Guy Whittal at 550 when he bowled Saqlain for 79.
He followed with the wicket of Waqar Younis on the next delivery before his brother Andrew Whittal ended Pakistan's innings with the wicket of Shahid Nazir.
Leg-spinner Paul Strang, who bore the brunt of punishment from Akram, finished with five for 212 from 69 overs.
